output.brief: The wrong expiry dates were not caused by the operators or the printer firmware. The printer job records show that from 4 October 22:10 onward, PackBridge sent a shelf life of 36 months instead of 24 for Veltranol. Operators did not override any of these jobs, and the printers printed exactly what was sent. The source is the ERP: on 3 October, a Regulatory Affairs edit under CC-309 changed the Veltranol shelf life to 36, but with a valid-from date of March 2027. The system applied it early. Earlier jobs after the firmware change and after the agency staff arrived were correct, so the operators and firmware are unlikely causes. I am fairly confident about the link to the ERP edit, less so about exactly why PackBridge used a future-dated value; that is not yet confirmed. The Site Director's plan to remove agency staff is unjustified and should not go ahead. Instead: reset the Veltranol shelf-life record now, extend the hold to all Veltranol lots packed since 4 October, including the two Line 1 lots in the warehouse, and add a second-person check of expiry at setup. Check the other products whose shelf-life records changed in October. Do not switch off the camera checks or over-label stock on assumption.
output.methodChoice: Collected two items: X12 (printer job records) and X2 (ERP shelf-life audit trail).
